subject: Why does INLA prediction time increase non-linearly?

messages.author: a51b9d9ec6729a87
messages.subject: Why does INLA prediction time increase non-linearly?
parts:
Hello,

I fit a hurdle model with a binomial and zeroinflatedpoisson0 likelihoods, and has produced what looks like some reasonable predictions. However, I noticed that the larger the prediction set, the increase in time for fitting increases non-linearly...perhaps more like exponentially, though not that dramatic.

Why would this be? In response, my strategy was to fit the model on the exact same training data 5 times, and include 1/5th of the prediction set in each iteration, yielding the full final set of predictions much more quickly. But there is no free lunch, and so I suspect my logic here is bad. Can someone correct me? I wonder if it has to do with the spatial component.

Regards,

Mark
